source.title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted II

teaching.hint: For which adjacent rows can a later column still change their lexicographic order?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A prior kept column that first makes one adjacent row smaller permanently settles that pair; only unsettled pairs constrain later columns.
solution_outline.approach: Scan columns left to right. Delete a column if it makes any unsettled adjacent pair decrease. Otherwise keep it and mark pairs with a strict increase as settled.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A pair is settled exactly when the kept prefix already orders it strictly. All unsettled pairs have equal kept prefixes.
solution_outline.correctness: A decreasing character in an unsettled pair would fix that pair in the wrong order, so deletion is forced. A safe column can only settle more pairs and never hurts, making keeping it optimal.
solution_outline.complexity: O(nm) time and O(n) auxiliary space for n rows of length m.
solution_outline.pitfall: Do not mark pairs settled until the whole column is known to be kept.

common_wrong_turns: Require each column itself to be sorted
Update settled state from a column later deleted
source_fidelity_notes: Clarifies that deletion affects every row and only the row sequence must be sorted.
